answer: For opaque whole milk, test in-line NIR diffuse reflection first with a flush-mounted probe, because transmission and transflection fail on thick, fat-rich milk. The earlier transmission-first answer is withdrawn. Calibrate protein with PLS against independent laboratory results, and keep MIR ATR as the comparison method.

inline.headline: Test NIR diffuse reflection in-line on the whole-milk line before the concentration stage
inline.install: In the whole-milk pipe before the concentration stage
inline.fiber: Silica Vis-NIR fiber (350–2400 nm), checked against the NIR range
inline.test_against: MIR ATR probe on the same samples
inline.not_final_because: Reflection readings depend on surface condition and fat globule size, protein calibration still needs independent laboratory references across the fat range, and the NIR range quoted to 2500 nm exceeds the 2400 nm fiber limit.

problems.text: The two-stream premise no longer applies: the client now describes one opaque whole-milk line, so one reflection-based interface is the test case, and a separate whey calibration is needed only if clear whey returns.
Transmission or transflection, the earlier first choice, cannot penetrate thick, fat-rich milk, so the earlier headline is withdrawn.
Reflection readings depend on surface condition and fat globule size, so the calibration must cover the fat range the line actually runs.
The NIR method is quoted up to 2500 nm but the silica Vis-NIR fiber is listed to 2400 nm, so the fiber must be checked against the wavelengths the model uses.

methods.why: Inline NIR reflection is the dairy method for opaque or concentrated products and is applied to fat and protein with scatter correction and PLS.
MIR gives well-defined absorption peaks and adds molecular specificity that NIR may miss, and ATR probes analyse liquids without sampling.
It relies on secondary emission from certain substances and most chemicals do not fluoresce, so it helps only if milk gives a usable signal.
It fails when milk is too thick or fat-rich, which is the case here.

experiment.objective: Test whether in-line NIR reflection tracks laboratory protein on the whole-milk line before the concentration stage.
steps: Flush-mount an NIR diffuse reflection probe in the whole-milk pipe before the concentration stage and record spectra over normal flow.
Take paired samples across the fat range and send them to an independent laboratory for protein.
Convert reflectance to absorbance, apply MSC or SNV, and build a PLS model for protein.
Validate on held-out samples taken on different days and compare with the laboratory values.
If NIR misses the client target, repeat with a MIR ATR probe on the same samples.
references: S01 p.17 (NIR reflection, MSC/SNV, PLS for fat and protein)
experiment.go_no_go: Accuracy and range criteria come from the client; none are set in the claims.

multispectral.why: Complementary information: NIR gives broad overlapping bands that need chemometrics, while MIR gives well-defined peaks and molecular specificity that NIR may miss.
multispectral.test: Compare NIR-only and fused NIR + MIR ATR PLS models on the same held-out laboratory-referenced samples; keep the fusion only if it beats the best single method.
